lines.text: In 1971, a man hijacked a plane, took two hundred thousand dollars, and jumped out into the night.
The FBI chased him for forty-five years, and never even learned his name.
But nine years later, a kid found some of the money. And it made everything stranger.
Thanksgiving Eve. A quiet man in a dark suit buys a twenty-dollar ticket with cash, and signs it Dan Cooper.
He sits in the last row, and hands the flight attendant a note.
She thinks it's his phone number.
So he whispers: Miss, you'd better look at that note. I have a bomb.
In his briefcase: red cylinders and wires.
He demands two hundred thousand dollars, and four parachutes.
He gets it all, in twenties. The FBI photographs every serial number.
Then he orders the pilots to Mexico City. Low, slow, landing gear down.
Somewhere over the forests of Washington, in the rain, in a trench coat and loafers, he lowers the rear stairs, and jumps.
He was never seen again.
No body. No parachute. Not one bill was ever spent.
And one of his parachutes was a dummy, sewn shut. It vanished with him.
Then, in 1980, an eight-year-old digging on a riverbank pulls out almost six thousand dollars of the ransom, still in rubber bands.
Miles from the forest. Nobody has ever proven how it got there.
The other hundred and ninety thousand? Never found.
In 2016, the FBI gave up. It's still the only unsolved hijacking in airline history.
So, did Dan Cooper survive? Comment your theory, and follow for more cases nobody solved.
